title: Kenyan Vanilla Cupcakes
community: Urban Kenya — the bakery and children's party staple
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Vanilla Cupcakes — moist, tender vanilla cupcakes frosted with a passion fruit-infused buttercream. The bakery staple of Nairobi — individually portioned celebration cakes that are as beautiful as they are delicious, with a Kenyan twist in the passion fruit frosting.
longDesc: Vanilla cupcakes with passion fruit frosting have become a Nairobi bakery signature — the cupcake itself is a moist, classic vanilla sponge, but the frosting incorporates fresh passion fruit juice for a tropical twist that is unmistakably Kenyan.
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line tin with cupcake liners.
Beat butter and sugar until pale — 4 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time. Add vanilla.
Alternate adding flour and milk in three additions.
Fill liners ⅔ full. Bake 18—20 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Make buttercream: beat butter until pale. Add icing sugar and passion fruit juice alternately. Beat until fluffy.
chefTips: Fill liners only ⅔ full — they rise significantly.
Completely cool before frosting — warm cupcakes melt the buttercream.
Passion fruit juice must be strained — seeds in the buttercream are unpleasant.
cookingScience: The ⅔ fill rule accounts for the CO2 expansion from baking powder during baking — cupcakes rise to form a dome above the liner. Over-filling causes overflow; under-filling produces flat-topped, dense cupcakes.
sustainabilityTips: Use locally produced eggs and butter — supporting Kenyan dairy farmers.
storage: Room temperature 3 days. Refrigerate frosted 4 days.
healthBenefits: Passion fruit adds vitamin C to the frosting.
culturalNote: Vanilla cupcakes with passion fruit frosting have become synonymous with Nairobi's bakery culture — the treat that appears at office birthdays, children's parties, and café display cases across the city.
